key_reasoning.reason: Base M: the per-scope list endpoints (GET /v1/settings/user, /project) are the closest pattern, but the change restructures their visibility rule into SettingsIndexService._scope_condition and ORs several scopes into one query. The existing per-scope endpoints now also run through list_scopes, so a dropped clause (admin_project_names, the project-budget alias hiding, the internal-prefix hiding) would expose other users' or projects' credential rows. Also new: the index_settings router's _parse_filters input validation (422 on malformed or too-deeply-nested JSON), the bigint OFFSET cap (MAX_PAGE) and the date-desc/id-asc tie-break ordering. The authorization red flag bumps it to L.

Three components across API and Service plus a read-only persistence query: the SettingsScope enum in the model, the new index_settings route with _parse_filters, and the SettingsIndexService list_scopes/_scope_condition/_query_postgres refactor. The visibility logic stays inside one service class rather than a cross-cutting utility, so the shared-utilities bump was not applied.

The diffstat reports 6 files (4-6 maps to M): 3 source files under rest_api/models, rest_api/routers and service/settings, the OpenAPI baseline, and 2 test files including a new real-engine (in-memory SQLite) visibility suite. That is about 787 insertions across the initial commits plus the fix-up.

Closest anchor is bundle M example epmcdme-10203 (REST endpoint with business logic, total 15). This diff matches it on layers and file count; Technical Risk is higher because of the authorization-sensitive visibility refactor, and Requirements Clarity is lower because the ticket fixed the scope set and ordering up front. The adjacent S example epmcdme-10102 (11) is narrower: 2 layers, 3 files, no authorization surface. No disagreement with the M band.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: affects authorization - per-scope visibility rules that gate which users' and projects' integration credentials are listed were refactored into a shared OR-combined SQL condition
